title: fix(deburr): start and exit picks for Deburr
body:
## What changed

This is slice 1 of #3329: the Deburr only. The Deburr now takes a start point and an exit point. The kind has a new pick capability, `PickCapability::Chain` (a point on an edge chain). The picks order the chains before any motion (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr_seam.rs`, `finishing3d::deburr_seamed`). The app Deburr arm passes `ChainSeam::of(picks, tool diameter)`.

The title uses `fix`, because the issue has the `bug` label (P2: the Deburr gives the user no control of the entry and the exit).

### Behaviour

- **Start:** the chain nearest the start pick is cut first.
  - An open chain starts at its end nearest the pick. It runs the other way when that end is its far end.
  - A closed chain is re-seated. It starts and ends at its point nearest the pick.
- **Exit:** the chain nearest the exit pick is cut last.
  - An open chain ends at its end nearest the pick.
  - A closed chain is re-seated at its point nearest the pick, so its lap ends there.
- **Start and exit on one closed chain (the only chain of the Deburr):** the chain starts at the start point and cuts its whole lap. Then it runs on along its own edges to the exit point. The run-on re-traces cut edges at the same depth.
- The other chains keep the automatic order between the first chain and the last chain.
- A pick with a Z is measured in 3D. A pick without a Z is measured in XY.
- The cut geometry does not change. Only the order and the direction change. `Toolpath::breaks` stays the automatic runs.
- With no pick, the output is the automatic ride, byte for byte.

### Refusals (by name, before any motion, never moved)

- A pick farther than 1.5 tool diameters from every chain: `start point (x, y) is d mm from the nearest edge chain of the Deburr, farther than the L mm ...`.
- An exit pick on an open chain, nearest the end where the start pick starts the chain: `exit point (...): the open edge chain that starts at the start point ends at its other end ...`.
- A start pick and an exit pick on one chain, while the Deburr has other chains (the #4168 review finding): `exit point (...): the start point and the exit point pick one edge chain, but the Deburr cuts N other edge chain(s) after the start chain ...`. That chain must be cut first and last, so the operation would end on another chain and move the exit. The rule closes the whole class: open and closed chains, any count of other chains. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/3329-deburr-picks.md`.
- A plunge column or a retract column at a chain end that a pick moved, where the column comes within the tool radius of the part: `start point (...): the plunge column to the edge at (...) comes within the tool radius r mm of the part ...`.
  - The check is exact: `stock_sim::dist_seg_tri` from the column segment to each facet. There is no sampling.
  - The column goes from one tool radius above the edge up to the clearance plane.
  - The check covers both moved ends of a reversed or re-seated chain. The refusal names the pick that moved the end. For example, an exit pick that reverses a chain moves its plunge, and that plunge is checked.
  - Only moved ends are checked. The automatic ride does not check its columns today, so the no-pick path stays byte for byte. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/3329-deburr-picks.md`.

### Mutation table

Each mutation was applied alone to `deburr_seam.rs`, then `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test deburr -- seam` was run.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | No column check (`columns(...)` not called) | RED: `a_moved_plunge_or_retract_column_under_an_overhang_is_refused`, `a_reversed_chain_checks_both_moved_ends` |
| M2 | Check only the end of the picked role (plunge for start, retract for exit) | RED: `a_reversed_chain_checks_both_moved_ends` |
| M3 | No reach law | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | No refusal of an exit at the start end of an open chain | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | No re-order of the chains | RED: `the_start_chain_is_cut_first_and_the_exit_chain_last` |
| M6 | No run-on from start to exit on one closed chain | RED: `start_and_exit_on_one_closed_chain_lap_then_run_on_to_the_exit` |
| M7 | Column check samples only the two ends of the column (not the exact segment distance) | RED: `a_moved_plunge_or_retract_column_under_an_overhang_is_refused`, `a_reversed_chain_checks_both_moved_ends` |
| M8 | No refusal of start and exit on one chain while other chains remain (the guard removed, the same as head 8fdf33ecc) | RED: `same_chain_picks_with_another_chain_must_keep_the_exit_or_refuse_it` (`exit silently moved from (5, 0, 3) to Point3 { x: 20.0, y: 0.0, z: 2.9999999999999996 }`); 9 pass, 1 fails |

## Readings

- App brick (40 x 40 x 10, `CM-0600-90`, 1 mm setback): a start at (20.5, 5, 10) gives the first plunge at (20, 5, 9). An exit at (5, -20.5) gives the last cut end at (5, -20, 9).
- Reach with the 6 mm cone: 9 mm. Column radius: 3 mm.

## Pinning tests

`camcraft-motion`, `tests/deburr.rs`, new module `deburr/seam.rs`. It joins the existing `deburr` suite, so no new test binary.
- `no_pick_is_the_automatic_ride_byte_for_byte`
- `a_start_pick_seats_the_closed_chain_at_its_nearest_point`
- `an_exit_pick_ends_the_closed_chain_at_its_nearest_point_and_rises_straight`
- `start_and_exit_on_one_closed_chain_lap_then_run_on_to_the_exit`
- `picks_on_an_open_chain_choose_its_direction`
- `the_start_chain_is_cut_first_and_the_exit_chain_last`
- `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_moved_plunge_or_retract_column_under_an_overhang_is_refused`
- `a_reversed_chain_checks_both_moved_ends`
- `same_chain_picks_with_another_chain_must_keep_the_exit_or_refuse_it` (two boxes, two closed rings: start and exit on one ring is refused by name; start and exit on the two rings ride)

Each test that keeps the geometry samples every cut move each 0.25 mm along its length, in both directions (picked against automatic, and automatic against picked).

`camcraft-app`, `tests/start_exit_shared.rs`, new module `start_exit_shared/deburr.rs`:
- `deburr_starts_at_the_picked_point_and_ends_at_the_picked_exit` (also: no pick gives the automatic path again)
- `deburr_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name`
- `deburr_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `get_job`, undo, redo, and the schema text)
- `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated: Deburr is `Chain`)

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The UI has no Deburr start / exit rows yet. The picks are set through MCP `edit_operation` and the project file, the same as the 5-axis slices. The "Not taken" line of the Deburr goes away.
- Multi-Axis Deburr is not changed. It still refuses a pick ("not taken").
- A Deburr with more than one pass (`passes > 1`): each pass uses the same seamed run. There is no dedicated pin.

## Remaining kinds of #3329

- 3D Pocket
- 3D Finish

## Gate

All runs are on head `77e8a02e75209101cdc6acf3e9555cb068dadd2e`. The log is `scratchpad/gates/4168-77e8a02e7.log`, and its first line is the head SHA.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 217 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (32.2 min). This includes `motion suites: deburr`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and `first_part_programs`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (7.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test deburr -- seam`: 10 passed.

The earlier head `8fdf33ecc` had the same gate green before this fix.

No heavy step: this is a P2 PR.

Changelog: Deburr takes a start point and an exit point: the chain nearest the start is cut first from its nearest end, the chain nearest the exit is cut last, and an impossible pick (also a start and an exit on one chain while other chains remain) is refused by name.
